clue.text: Gang with silver on vehicle

parts.note: a gang is a group of people, a band
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A gang of thieves loads silver into a getaway vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is taken literally here, supplying its own two letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon was a wagon carrying a band in a parade, so it is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Fraudulent knight taken out of commission for good

indicators.note: taken out of with for says one letter leaves the commission and another replaces it

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment, like a commission
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A fake knight is struck off the commission for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means sham or fake, as fraudulent does.

clue.text: Raced over to judge to tell the story

indicators.note: over says the word for raced is turned back

parts.note: raced means ran
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: Someone races over to the judge to give an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount a sequence of events.

clue.text: Fantasist from Spooner's island, amusing to listen to

indicators.note: Spooner's says the first sounds of two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: Malta is a Mediterranean island
witty means amusing

explanation.surface: A daydreamer claims his island tales are entertaining to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts gives WALTA MITTY, which 'to listen to' says only sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of James Thurber's story, and his name is used for any fantasist.

clue.text: Doctor's entertaining chat over a brandy

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the doctor surrounds the chat

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rap is slang for talk or chat

explanation.surface: A doctor chats with a patient over a glass of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like amusing; here it means holding as a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace.

clue.text: Peer, person of high social position, attending race venue briefly

parts.note: nob is British slang for a toff or upper-class person

indicators.note: briefly says the last letter of the race venue is cut

parts.note: Le Mans in France hosts the famous 24-hour motor race

explanation.surface: A peer and a socialite attend a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, a titled man.

clue.text: Michelangelo's sculpture, Grandma

definitions.meaning: Michelangelo carved a famous marble statue of the Hebrew prophet for the tomb of Pope Julius II
Grandma ... was the American folk painter who began painting in her late seventies

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same surname: the prophet in marble and the elderly American folk artist.

clue.text: Old lady eating duck, old bird

indicators.note: eating says the mother takes in the duck

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: An old woman tucks into duck, an elderly bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' wants to be the meal; it is the zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, extinct for centuries.

clue.text: Popular resort area for treatment of disease

indicators.note: treatment of says the letters of disease are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A popular resort is promoted as a cure for illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast where holidaymakers go is a classic popular resort area.

clue.text: Two items of clothing for fielder

parts.note: shorts are an item of clothing
a top is the second item of clothing

explanation.surface: A fielder's kit is just two garments.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the shortstop is the fielder between second and third base.

clue.text: Something of a thug, or, I'll add, an ape

indicators.note: Something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describes a thug and adds a parting insult comparing him to an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the great apes, native to central African forests.

clue.text: Show of boldness from supporter — see trouble ensuing

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear that supports
v. abbreviates Latin vide, meaning see, in references
ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A backer of a cause sees trouble coming and puts on a bold front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensuing' just tells you ADO follows the earlier pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering display of courage, often hollow.

clue.text: Small old man in health resort

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
one's old man is one's father, pa

explanation.surface: A small elderly man takes the waters at a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with mineral springs where people go for health treatments is a spa.

clue.text: Pick up on word in elevator

indicators.note: in this across clue, on means placed after the earlier piece

parts.note: to word something is to put it into words, to express it
to pick something up is to lift it

explanation.surface: Someone picks up on a particular word used inside a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: An express lift is a fast elevator that skips the lower floors; 'elevator' is the American name for a lift.

clue.text: Bird and dog and butterfly

parts.note: the swallow is a migrating bird
to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: A list of creatures: a bird, a dog and a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' wants to be the animal; it is the verb to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowtails are large butterflies named for their forked hind wings.

clue.text: Sordid around Turkey's capital, like the baths there?

indicators.note: around says the sordid word wraps about the next letter

parts.note: seamy means sordid or disreputable, as in the seamy side of life

indicators.note: a word's capital is its first, capital letter

explanation.surface: A sordid tale set around Istanbul's bathhouses, which are hot and steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's capital' wants to be Ankara; it is the letter T. The definition then refers back to Turkey: Turkish baths are hot and humid.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish baths are full of vapour, so a fitting description of them is full of steam.

clue.text: Toady, extremely smarmy chap, not replaced

indicators.note: extremely picks the outer letters of the word smarmy
replaced says the letters of chap and not are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A creep is described as an extremely smarmy fellow who was not replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a flatterer who toadies to the powerful.

clue.text: Scottish solicitor, a wit during season

indicators.note: during says the wit sits inside the season

parts.note: Lent is the season of fasting before Easter
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A Scottish solicitor turns out to be a comedian in the Lenten season.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a law agent was the formal title for a solicitor acting in court matters.

clue.text: Staff shortly to receive notice it's heartless and cruel

indicators.note: to receive says the shortened staff takes the other pieces inside
shortly says the stick loses its final letter

parts.note: a staff is a stick
an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of it's

parts.note: it's taken as its letters, ITS

explanation.surface: Staff are told shortly that a notice is coming, a heartless and cruel act.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain, so the adjective means cruel.

clue.text: About to drink gin or cobblers

parts.note: C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Someone is about to have a glass of gin, or talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' wants to be the spirit; it is a gin trap. 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, from rhyming slang 'cobbler's awls'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: One failing to gain a place in a lyceum, at first so put out

definitions.text: One failing to gain a place

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letters of the words a and lyceum

parts.note: to run a story is to put it out, publish it

explanation.surface: A school pupil fails to win a place and is upset at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse that finishes outside the placings, and by extension any loser.

clue.text: Lose temper and go off

definitions.meaning: to explode, as a bomb does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to erupt in anger and to explode.

clue.text: Prime minister not returned after successes

indicators.note: after says the reversed word follows the successes

parts.note: wins are successes

indicators.note: returned says the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister failed to return after his victories.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's wartime Prime Minister.

clue.text: Wreck left in wide bay

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside the bay

parts.note: a bight is a broad curving bay

explanation.surface: A shipwreck is left in a wide bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or ruin it, as disease ruins crops.

clue.text: Cat and bat in a tree

parts.note: pussy is a familiar word for a cat
cricket bats are made from willow, so willow stands for the bat

explanation.surface: A cat and a bat are both up in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A small willow whose soft furry catkins resemble a cat's fur; it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Keep on at its head to name the pub

definitions.meaning: to keep on at someone is to pester or harass them

definitions.text: its head to name the pub
definitions.meaning: the ... Head is a common British pub name, so add 'S HEAD to this word and you name the pub

explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone repeatedly is to badger them, and the old horse gives its name to many British pubs.

clue.text: Turned up to search a lake

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, says the word for search is read upwards

parts.note: to drag a lake or river is to search it with nets or hooks

explanation.surface: Something turned up when they searched a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like found; it reverses DRAG to GARD. Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Garda is the largest of the Italian lakes, so the proper name is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Perhaps John Lennon tune piano or trumpet initially required

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word trumpet

explanation.surface: A John Lennon song needs a piano or trumpet part to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: John Lennon looks like the musician; he names Liverpool John Lennon Airport, so 'Perhaps' flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's airport is named after the Beatle, so the name is an example of an aviation hub.

clue.text: Not allowed in the shops

definitions.meaning: an idea that is ruled ... or forbidden
a new book or record that has been released is available to buy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ruled out and newly released for sale.

clue.text: Greek looking for hard worker

parts.note: to be after something is to be looking for it

explanation.surface: A Greek is searching for a diligent employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is British slang for hard work, so someone who toils diligently is a grafter.

clue.text: Opinion expressed by third of guests entering marquee

indicators.note: entering says the picked letter goes inside the marquee

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word guests

explanation.surface: A view is put forward by one of the guests arriving at the marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held by a person or group.

clue.text: A pile of cards found in bureau depicting a region of Spain

indicators.note: found in says the pile sits inside the bureau

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, a bureau of sorts
in card games the talon is the stock of undealt cards

explanation.surface: A pack of cards discovered in a writing desk bears a picture of a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bureau' wants to be a desk; it is the agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern autonomous community of Spain, capital Barcelona.
